code: # Full weight within `plateau` minutes, Gaussian decay beyond plateau_kernel <- decay_kernel(   function(distance, sigma, plateau) {     ifelse(       distance <= plateau,       1,       exp(-(distance - plateau)^2 / (2 * sigma^2))     )   },   name = "plateau",   parameter = "scale",   args = list(plateau = 3) ) plateau_kernel <spax_decay_kernel> plateau sigma: scale bounds on sigma: 0 to Inf defined at distance 0: yes smooth in sigma: yes fixed arguments: plateau = 3 function: function (distance, sigma, plateau)  {     ifelse(distance <= plateau, 1, exp(-(distance - plateau)^2/(2 *          sigma^2))) } plateau_model <- clm_allocation(   inputs = inputs,   family = plateau_kernel,  # a declaration instead of "gaussian"   fit_v0 = TRUE )  plateau_fit <- fit_allocation(   model = plateau_model,   observed = observed,   starts = starts,   lower = c(sigma = 0.5, v0 = 1e-6),   upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 10),   output = "flow",   loss = "poisson",   gradient = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8) ) coef(plateau_fit) sigma         v0  3.88744084 0.05433508 # Loss differences are measured from the first fit, the Gaussian comparison <- compare_allocations(   fits = list(gaussian = fit, plateau = plateau_fit),   models = list(gaussian = model, plateau = plateau_model) ) as.data.frame(comparison)[   c("specification", "parameters", "loss_difference", "count_correlation") ] specification              parameters loss_difference count_correlation 1      gaussian sigma=4.591, v0=0.02733            0.00         0.8846533 2       plateau sigma=3.887, v0=0.05434        62248.12         0.8464323

code: units <- list(   demand_units = "requests",   demand_period = "one_reference_period",   supply_units = "service_slots",   supply_period = "one_reference_period",   travel_units = "minutes" )  # Travel minutes between 80 origins and 40 facilities on a wavy strip i <- seq_len(80) j <- seq_len(40) boot_travel <- sqrt(   outer(seq(2, 58, length.out = 80), seq(4, 56, length.out = 40), "-")^2 +   outer(8 * sin(i * .73), 7 * sin(j * 1.31), "-")^2) + 2 dimnames(boot_travel) <- list(paste0("origin", i), paste0("facility", j))  # Demand at each origin and supply at each facility boot_demand <- setNames(80 + 35 * (1 + sin(i * .23)), rownames(boot_travel)) boot_supply <- setNames(rep(c(5, 7, 6, 8, 9), 8), colnames(boot_travel))  # True choice probabilities under the static CLM truth <- c(sigma = 12, v0 = 45) boot_score <- exp(-boot_travel^2 / (2 * truth[["sigma"]]^2)) *   rep(boot_supply, each = length(boot_demand)) boot_probability <- boot_score / (rowSums(boot_score) + truth[["v0"]])  # Observed facility totals: independent Poisson counts around the truth set.seed(2490001) boot_observed <- setNames(   rpois(40, colSums(boot_probability * boot_demand)),   names(boot_supply) )  # Prepare, declare and fit, as for Cornwall boot_inputs <- prepare_allocation(   demand = boot_demand,   supply = boot_supply,   distance = boot_travel,   metadata = units ) boot_model <- clm_allocation(boot_inputs, family = "gaussian", fit_v0 = TRUE) boot_starts <- rbind(   short = c(sigma = 8, v0 = 25),   medium = c(sigma = 15, v0 = 70),   wide = c(sigma = 25, v0 = 15) ) boot_fit <- fit_allocation(   model = boot_model,   observed = boot_observed,   starts = boot_starts,   lower = c(sigma = 2, v0 = 1),   upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 500),   output = "utilization",  # facility totals   loss = "poisson",   gradient = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8) ) rbind(truth = truth, estimate = coef(boot_fit)) sigma       v0 truth    12.00000 45.00000 estimate 13.27962 48.57499

code: # Demand and travel grids at `factor` times the native cell width at_resolution <- function(factor) {   # Native grid: unchanged   if (factor == 1) return(list(demand = pop, travel = travel))    # Finer grid: split residents evenly, copy the parent's travel times   if (factor < 1) {     k <- round(1 / factor)     return(list(demand = disagg(pop, k) / k^2, travel = disagg(travel, k)))   }    # Coarser grid: add up residents, take resident-weighted mean minutes   demand <- aggregate(pop, factor, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)   minutes <- aggregate(travel * pop, factor, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE) /     demand   list(demand = demand, travel = minutes) }  factors <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4) inputs <- lapply(factors, at_resolution) # The E2SFCA of the other guides, for one resolution fca <- function(x) {   spax_e2sfca(     demand = x$demand,     supply = gp,     distance = x$travel,     decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),     demand_normalize = "identity",     id_col = "practice",     supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg"   ) }  # Median elapsed seconds of three runs at each resolution seconds <- sapply(inputs, function(x) {   median(replicate(3, system.time(fca(x))[["elapsed"]])) })  results <- lapply(inputs, fca) # The native surface and residents, one value per native cell native <- 1000 * values(results[[2]]$accessibility, mat = FALSE) residents <- values(pop, mat = FALSE)  # One table row per resolution summary_row <- function(k) {   # This surface on the native grid, and its own cells' residents and area   a <- 1000 * resample(results[[k]]$accessibility, pop, method = "near")   a <- values(a, mat = FALSE)   d <- values(inputs[[k]]$demand, mat = FALSE)   area <- values(cellSize(inputs[[k]]$demand, unit = "km"), mat = FALSE)    # Index per 1,000 on its own grid, and the change from the native surface   own <- 1000 * values(results[[k]]$accessibility, mat = FALSE)   change <- abs(a / native - 1)    data.frame(     factor = factors[k],     cell_km2 = round(mean(area[!is.na(d)]), 2),     populated_cells = sum(!is.na(d)),     residents = round(sum(d, na.rm = TRUE)),     seconds = seconds[k],     mean_per_1000 = round(weighted.mean(own, d, na.rm = TRUE), 3),     median_abs_change_pct = round(       100 * median(change[!is.na(residents)], na.rm = TRUE),       1     ),     weighted_abs_change_pct = round(       100 * weighted.mean(change, residents, na.rm = TRUE),       1     )   ) }  comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(factors), summary_row))  # Every resolution keeps the same residents, to within one person stopifnot(max(abs(comparison$residents - comparison$residents[2])) <= 1) comparison factor cell_km2 populated_cells residents seconds mean_per_1000 1    0.5     0.14           27648    541184   0.282         0.575 2    1.0     0.55            6912    541184   0.061         0.575 3    2.0     2.20            1829    541184   0.015         0.575 4    4.0     8.79             506    541184   0.010         0.575   median_abs_change_pct weighted_abs_change_pct 1                   0.0                     0.0 2                   0.0                     0.0 3                   1.8                     1.4 4                   3.3                     2.5 # The native surface and the 4 x 4 surface, both on the native grid pair <- c(   1000 * results[[2]]$accessibility,   resample(1000 * results[[4]]$accessibility, pop, method = "near") ) names(pair) <- c("Native grid", "Aggregated 4 x 4")  plot(   pair,   axes = FALSE,   col = hcl.colors(50, "viridis"),   range = range(values(pair), na.rm = TRUE),   mar = c(1, 1, 2, 6),   plg = list(title = "GP FTE\nper 1,000") )

code: library(terra)  # Distances on a small 10 x 10 grid r <- rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = 0, ymax = 10) values(r) <- 1:100  # Built-in decay functions w <- c(   calc_decay(r, method = "gaussian", sigma = 30),   calc_decay(r, method = "exponential", sigma = 0.1),   calc_decay(r, method = "power", sigma = 2),   calc_decay(r, method = "binary", sigma = 50) ) names(w) <- c("gaussian", "exponential", "power", "binary") plot(w)   # A custom decay function receives the distances and its own arguments gaussian_power <- function(distance, sigma = 30, power = 2, ...) {   exp(-(distance^2) / (2 * sigma^2)) * distance^(-power) } w_custom <- calc_decay(r, method = gaussian_power, sigma = 30, power = 1.5)  # A declared kernel records its meaning, bounds and fixed arguments plateau <- decay_kernel(   function(distance, sigma, plateau = 5) {     ifelse(distance <= plateau, 1, exp(-(distance - plateau)^2 / (2 * sigma^2)))   },   name = "plateau", parameter = "scale", args = list(plateau = 5) ) w_plateau <- calc_decay(r, method = plateau, sigma = 10)  # One layer per facility gives one layer of weights per facility distances <- rast(replicate(3, r)) names(distances) <- c("facility1", "facility2", "facility3") weights <- calc_decay(distances, method = "gaussian", sigma = 30)

title: Declare the Huff model over checked allocation inputs — huff_allocation
code: # Mainland Cornwall: small areas share their registered residents among the # practices in proportion to attractiveness times travel-time decay. areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ]) gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ]) travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]  # Without an outside option, demand is the residents registered at the # mainland practices demand <- stats::setNames(areas$registered_in, areas$lsoa) supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice) inputs <- prepare_allocation(demand, supply, travel)  # Power decay with a fitted attractiveness exponent model <- huff_allocation(inputs)  # Evaluate at given parameters: distance exponent 2, attractiveness # exponent 1 evaluate_allocation(model, c(sigma = 2, beta = 1)) #> <allocation evaluation> #> converged: TRUE #> iterations: 1 #> error: 0 #> residual_norm: 0  # Fit practice totals of registrations from two starts totals <- tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$practice, sum) observed <- stats::setNames(numeric(ncol(travel)), colnames(travel)) observed[intersect(names(totals), names(observed))] <-   totals[intersect(names(totals), names(observed))] fit <- fit_allocation(   model, observed,   starts = rbind(a = c(sigma = 1, beta = 0.5), b = c(sigma = 3, beta = 1.5)),   lower = c(sigma = 0.1, beta = 0.05), upper = c(sigma = 10, beta = 5),   loss = "poisson" ) fit$best$theta #>     sigma      beta  #> 1.0415962 0.6062301

title: Prepare data for a spax model — prep_data
code: # Mainland Cornwall: registered residents, GP FTE and travel minutes areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ]) gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ]) demand <- stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa) supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice) travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice] prep_data(demand, supply, travel,           metadata = list(demand_units = "registered residents",                           supply_units = "GP FTE", travel_units = "minutes")) #> <spax data> 336 origins (336 active) x 54 facilities #>   demand      604,471 registered residents #>   supply      GP FTE #>   travel      minutes; unknown for 0 active origins #>   policies    missing demand: error; missing travel: error  # Raster data for a floating catchment area index pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif") grid_data <- prep_data(pop, sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp), travel_grid,                        id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg") grid_data #> <spax data> raster 132 x 271 cells x 55 facilities; supply gp_fte_extg #>   demand    1 layer; travel 55 layers #>   note      holds terra rasters: prepare the data again after saveRDS() spax(grid_data, spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10))) #> <spax access> E2SFCA, 1 layer on 132 x 271 cells #>  #> Spatial Properties: #> - Resolution: 0.00833333 x 0.00833333 #> - Dimensions: 132 x 271 #>  #> Measures: 1 #> - gp_fte_extg #>  #> Facilities: 55 #>  #> Parameters: #> - Decay function: gaussian (sigma = 10) #> - Demand normalization: identity   # \donttest{ # An allocation model on the mainland grid, fitted to practice totals. Demand # must count the same people as the totals: residents registered with a GP # practice. The grid estimates residents in 2020, fewer than the registered # residents of the mainland small areas, so it is scaled to them and gives # only where they live. mainland <- terra::ext(-6, terra::xmax(pop), terra::ymin(pop), terra::ymax(pop)) pop <- terra::crop(pop, mainland) registered <- pop * sum(areas$registered) /   terra::global(pop, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]] d_mainland <- prep_data(registered, gp,                         terra::crop(travel_grid[[gp$practice]], mainland),                         id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg")  # Registrations of mainland residents at the mainland practices flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &                           cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ] totals <- obs_totals(tapply(flows$patients, flows$practice, sum))  # The cells with residents become the origins. The Huff model (power decay, # fitted attractiveness exponent) is well determined by these totals. huff <- spax(d_mainland, spec_huff(), observed = totals) huff #> <spax allocation> Huff model (no outside option) #>   decay       power (sigma = exponent): fit #>   attraction  (kappa * supply)^beta: kappa = 1, beta = fit #>   outside     none #>   data        6,912 origins x 54 facilities #>  #>   parameter  value   status #>   sigma      1.059   fitted #>   beta       0.6123  fitted #>   v0         0       held #>   kappa      1       held #>  #>   selected    scan1 (start 1 of 3); 3 of 3 starts converged #>   boundary    none #>   starts      default search, 15 of 15 grid points, loss poisson  # What the totals say about travel: the fit against no decay check_fit(huff) #> <allocation check> #>     comparator     loss loss_difference contact trip_median trip_p90 #>         fitted -5042045               0       1          11       53 #>       no_decay -5038257            3788       1          40       85 #>  capacity_only -5038282            3763      NA          40       85 #> Trip lengths are one-way, in travel units, weighted by expected flows. #>  #> The fitted allocation reproduces the counts better than both comparators. # }

text: spax_2sfca, spax_e2sfca spax_m2sfca remain supported public FCA entry points; compute_access also retained. experimental spax_3sfca spax_huff2sfca add selection weights divide origin's demand among facilities. take raster demand facility travel layers. Multiple supply columns produce independent accessibility indicators, interacting resource constraints. experimental allocation interface runs model one call: spax binds model specification (spec_clm spec_huff, decay decay_gaussian) data prep_data, fits counts declared obs_flows obs_totals, evaluates every parameter value. spax_clm spax_huff raw inputs. title: Calculate Original Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (2SFCA) accessibility scores — spax_2sfca
text: original Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (2SFCA) method operates two steps: Step 1: facility j: * Define catchment area within threshold distance/time * Sum population demand locations within catchment * Calculate supply--demand ratio Rj = Sj/sum(Pi) Step 2: demand location : * Define catchment area within threshold distance/time * Sum facility ratios Rj within catchment * Final accessibility score Ai = sum(Rj) Key characteristics: 1. Binary catchment areas (within threshold = 1, beyond = 0) 2. Equal weights locations within catchment 3. normalization demand weights 4. Single threshold value steps Limitations addressed later methods: * distance decay within catchments * Artificial barriers catchment boundaries * Potential demand overestimation overlapping areas

text: E2SFCA method enhances original 2SFCA introducing: Step 1: facility j: * Weight demand points distance decay: Wd(dij) * Calculate supply--demand ratio Rj = Sj/sum(Pi * Wd(dij)) Step 2: demand location : * Weight facility ratios distance decay: Wr(dij) * Calculate accessibility score Ai = sum(Rj * Wr(dij)) Key improvements original 2SFCA: 1. Distance decay within catchments 2. Differentiated travel behavior demand vs. access phases 3. code: # Load example data library(terra) library(sf)  # Cornwall population grid and travel time to each GP practice pop_rast <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")  # Drop geometry for supply data gp <- cornwall_gp |> st_drop_geometry()  # Calculate accessibility with Gaussian decay result <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(     method = "gaussian",     sigma = 10 # 10-minute characteristic travel time   ),   demand_normalize = "semi", # Prevent demand inflation   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" )  # Extract and plot accessibility surface plot(result$accessibility, main = "GP Accessibility (E2SFCA)")   # Access facility-level information head(result$facilities) #>       id gp_fte_extg #> 1 L82001   10.298887 #> 2 L82003    4.693333 #> 3 L82004    4.341333 #> 4 L82006    7.973333 #> 5 L82007    2.888800 #> 6 L82008    4.670400  # Compare different decay functions result_exp <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(     method = "exponential",     sigma = 0.1   ),   demand_normalize = "semi",   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" )  # Plot both for comparison plot(c(result$accessibility, result_exp$accessibility),   main = c("Gaussian Decay", "Exponential Decay") )   # Two demand groups that compete for the same practices, with a fixed # illustrative split of the population and a decay scale for each group groups <- list(younger = pop_rast * 0.6, older = pop_rast * 0.4) result_groups <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = groups,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(     younger = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 8),     older = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 15)   ),   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" ) names(result_groups$accessibility) #> [1] "gp_fte_extg.younger" "gp_fte_extg.older"   "gp_fte_extg.all"     result_groups$parameters$groups #> [1] "younger" "older"   plot(result_groups$accessibility)

text: Patch release. Poisson flow fits now maximum likelihood estimates; saved fits 0.3.0 keep working. Poisson fits fit_allocation() now floor modelled counts 1e-250 instead 1e-9 (set loss_args = list(eps = ...)). old floor capped loss positive counts model puts almost weight , residents registered far home, flow fit Poisson maximum likelihood estimate moved floor: Cornwall registration guide Gaussian scale changes 4.36 4.59 minutes outside weight 0.0176 0.0273. Facility-total estimates unaffected. fit_allocation() warns check_allocation() reports cells positive counts still modelled floor (example counts absent edges facility zero supply); check_allocation() also reports saved fits made old floor. compare_allocations() treats saved Poisson fit without stored floor using 1e-9, compares fits different floors neither floor changes either loss. title: spax 0.3.0
text: First release includes experimental allocation workflow. Experimental functions may change later versions; record package version reproducing analysis. Fixed: loss = "poisson" gradient = TRUE, analytic gradient now gradient floored loss. modelled count floor (eps, 1e-9) adds constant loss, now adds nothing gradient; , kept slope 1 - y / eps, misled optimizer flow targets positive counts model puts almost flow (starts stopped apart, line-search failures). Fits whose modelled counts stay floor unchanged; Poisson loss unchanged, saved fits keep working. New experimental decay_kernel() declares distance decay kernel plain data: built-kernel name, function distance sigma, kept exact text code (comments layout kept) together name, label sigma means, bounds sigma fixed extra arguments. function run grid distances declared, one returns weights finite, nonnegative non-increasing refused. declaration can replace method string calc_decay() decay_params FCA functions (spax_e2sfca(), spax_m2sfca(), spax_3sfca() spax_huff2sfca()); built-declaration behaves exactly like string. clm_allocation() accepts declared kernel family. Fitting, evaluation, requested-location prediction, check_allocation() compare_allocations() work , bootstrap_allocation() kernel smooth sigma. kernel declared smooth = FALSE (cutoff step, example) can evaluated used prediction fitted. Results use declared kernel save code new version prediction snapshot (spax_clm_prediction_v2), using saved fit runs code saved fits read sources trust. Snapshots built-kernels unchanged. Printed summarized fits now label sigma meaning kernel, example gaussian (sigma = travel scale). declared kernel held checks. function must elementwise (weight distance may depend distances order), receives vector matrix distances. sigma must positive, well inside declared bounds, calc_decay(), fitting evaluation, requested-location prediction saved snapshot read (“ decay requires positive sigma”). check declaration also runs function positive lower bound finite upper bound sigma, calc_decay() refuses negative non-finite weight finite distance, grid declaration rule . SpatRaster read memory declared kernel applied . finite-difference derivatives fitting bootstrap_allocation() use longer step outside bounds model’s parameters. Next bound, example lower bound declared kernel, use one-sided difference. central step used leave bounds : fit fell back analytic gradient without message, bootstrap_allocation() stop error theta outside bounds lose draws lie bound. Results built-kernels change, except parameter closer zero one step (1e-6) longer errors. score diagnostic original fit computed, bootstrap_allocation() now refuses intervals status original_score_failed instead stopping. Fitting keeps trial parameter values inside bounds model’s parameters estimate inside search bounds, also exp(log(bound)) rounds just outside bound (example 7.6). fit search bound refused bootstrap_allocation() boundary estimate instead failing “invalid saved fit bounds”, declared kernel can fitted declared bound. estimates change. bootstrap_allocation() adds coverage_note result, prints , every model built-Gaussian decay fitted sigma v0 kappa beta equal 1, case coverage study covered: kernels, fitted beta values kappa beta use procedure without separate coverage study. Results studied case unchanged note. New experimental spax_3sfca() computes three-step floating catchment area index. origin first divides demand among facilities selection weights, facility’s share origin’s decay weights, steps use product decay selection weights. selection weights can use different decay one weights distance (selection_params). steps share one kernel, index returns total supply facilities gather demand. New experimental spax_huff2sfca() calculation Huff selection probabilities, also depend facility attractiveness (default single supply measure; alpha exponent). alpha = 0 equals spax_3sfca(). Several supply measures need explicit attractiveness. New experimental calc_demand() computes demand population groups (example age bands) group-specific rates, times common scale. total-population grid, cell’s group composition applied total, reconciles gridded group total products sum exactly. New experimental calc_travel_time() computes continuous least-cost travel times facilities every cell analysis grid friction surface (Malaria Atlas Project motorized friction surface), optional barriers, maximum time bilinear averaging transfer friction surface grid. result origin--facility matrix prepare_allocation() accepts, matching cell index, one raster layer per facility. New experimental compare_allocations() summarizes several fitted allocations side side (contact, capacity per contact, spread contact, agreement observed counts loss) , zones, lists zones whose reporting class changes. Loss differences reported observed targets, loss, demand, supply travel times identical; travel times verified models supplied. Saved coverage also gains .data.frame(type = "zones", zones = ...), aggregates cells zones demand contacting-demand weights. New experimental check_allocation() compares fitted allocation allocation without distance decay (within prepared travel support) one shares counts capacity alone, loss, reports one-way trip lengths implies. capacity closely tracks observed facility counts, counts alone may identify distance decay; check says instead leaving discovered. fitted attractiveness exponent re-optimized comparators. reports never changes fit. -decay comparator check_allocation() exact: model constant kernel (weight 1 every finite travel time), whatever kernel model uses, instead built-kernel extreme parameter value. reported parameters longer include sigma, allocation use: parameters$no_decay holds re-optimized parameters sigma, table reads decay, followed re-optimized v0 (beta) model fits . Reported losses move 1e-8 relative travel times minutes. summary.spax() coverage now counts cells value, cells outside study area (sea) longer lower , reports share cells accessibility zero. previously divided number cells value every cell raster. Printed corrected CLM fits now show model: clm instead internal family name huff. fit saved saveRDS() read back longer rejected bootstrap_allocation() reported like like compare_allocations() package keeps source references (development load, R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE=yes). saved copy package’s Poisson loss function differed original references, comparison now ignores. calc_decay(), sample_pmf() rasterize_demand() examples now run; last uses Cornwall small areas. README guides now use bundled Cornwall GP data, real maps, instead generated grids. facility bootstrap guide keeps generated network, true parameters known. guides now follow one reader journey. vignette("spax") short Get started guide; new vignette("cornwall-data") introduces example data , data-prep; FCA guides fca-methods, e2sfca-steps grid-resolution (formerly spax-101 spax-104); allocation track runs model-choice allocation-workflow separate facility-bootstrap guide. pkgdown site groups articles headings sets printed output apart code. Breaking: Thailand Health Region 12 example data removed package, redistribution terms fully confirmed. examples tests now use open Cornwall GP data. package 1 MB instead 27 MB. Analyses need old objects load saved copy earlier spax version. transform_pmf(), transform_likelihood() transform_demand() now accept SpatVector input. column check read one-column data frame, every column rejected; extent check also rejected single collinear points. transform_demand(full_output = TRUE) longer requires undocumented id column, transform_demand() now warns area covers grid cell, count dropped. Fixes FCA PMF tools: rasterize_demand() without prior now uses documented uniform prior non-missing cells template’s first layer. previously used observations’ PMF, posterior proportional squared counts. standardize = TRUE now refused, z-scores likelihood, -missing template. update_pmf(normalize = FALSE, density = TRUE) longer scales posterior twice. Point input transform_pmf(), transform_likelihood() rasterize_demand() now adds points fall cell, ignoring missing values; last point’s value kept, counts lost. Polygon values still copied every cell cover. transform_pmf(), update_pmf() rasterize_demand() accept multi-layer rasters normalize layer separately; previously failed “condition length > 1”. update_pmf() requires matching layer counts unless one side single layer. sample_pmf() takes size rounded total raw density input, documented, prob given; PMF input still needs size. Multi-layer input refused clear message. calc_normalize() refuses missing numeric ref_value (NA_real_, NaN) clear error instead base R error. calc_normalize() SpatRaster accepts numeric ref_value "reference" method; previously failed inside terra::ifel(). documentation now states rasters normalized cell cell across layers. calc_decay() accepts integer distances 1:5; logical matrices classed numerics units objects refused. summary.spax() keeps every requested quantile (kept first), custom quantiles print percentage labels. sample_pmf() rejects n single non-negative whole number (also snap mode) instead returning empty raster drawing truncated count, -NA input gets PMF error instead base R error. spax_2sfca() validates threshold message names ; NA NULL, gave -NaN results binary default, refused. print() FCA result whose decay_params$method function longer fails cat(); prints custom function, declared kernel prints name. print() FCA result whose decay_params$sigma raster (variable catchment) longer fails sprintf(); prints variable (raster). calc_normalize() calc_choice() now refuse negative weights (outside snap mode); previously divided remaining sum returned negative “probabilities”. custom calc_normalize() method still receives input unchecked. clm_allocation() requires fit_v0 fit_beta TRUE FALSE; values "yes" silently treated FALSE. ?calc_decay documents kernel’s formula sigma used none given, notes power decay infinite distance 0. fit_allocation() bootstrap_allocation() longer force full garbage collection every fit: internal fit timer used system.time(), collects garbage first default. Results unchanged; repeated fits run faster (package tests take half long). update_pmf(), transform_demand() calc_normalize() examples now run; first two previously referred undefined object. allocation-workflow vignette now loads full 399-attempt bootstrap result vignettes/allocation-bootstrap.rds instead recomputing , cutting vignette rebuild 200 s 30 s. printed call, seed every reported number unchanged; vignette stops stored result match live fit. Regenerate data-raw/precompute-vignette-bootstrap.R whenever bootstrap fitting code changes. test now runs real bootstrap engine three attempts. New open example data 55 GP practices NHS Cornwall Isles Scilly: cornwall_gp, cornwall_lsoa, cornwall_flows, cornwall_travel, cornwall_pop.tif cornwall_gp_travel.tif grids read read_spax_example(). sources openly licensed (Open Government Licence v3.0, Creative Commons Attribution); see inst/COPYRIGHTS. data rebuilt reproducibly data-raw/cornwall_gp.R pinned sources. supported minimum R 4.4.0, testthat 3.2.0 tests. dependency testing policy development branch. CI targets release R Linux, Windows macOS, plus Linux R-devel exact minimum R version. Existing public FCA calling semantics unchanged compatibility floor. Tutorials now use portable generated examples; live routing optional executed routine builds. model-choice guide connects public FCA experimental allocation workflows. full allocation example retains 399 bootstrap attempts existing statistical reporting rules. Removed unused bench fasterize packages Suggests portable tutorial conversion. Public FCA functions remain supported, including independent accessibility indicators multiple supply columns. equations normalization choices unchanged experimental allocation interface. Six experimental functions provide corrected static CLM workflow: prepare_allocation(), clm_allocation(), fit_allocation(), evaluate_allocation(), predict_allocation() bootstrap_allocation(). Preparation checks IDs, units declarations support. Fitting retains explicit starts diagnostics; prediction uses saved facility loads. Allocation probabilities, modeled counts supply attribution distinct meanings. Requested predictions distinguish unknown travel absent connections expose validity support flags. conditional facility-case bootstrap supports static CLM fitted outside mass, fitted complete whole facility counts. decay kernel can built declared, smooth sigma, beta can fixed fitted. intervals require declared observation assumptions complete 399-attempt run; refusals, failed attempts incomplete results remain available inspection. Coverage evaluated Gaussian decay fitted sigma v0; kernels fitted beta use procedure without separate coverage study. Saved-result methods provide parameter, bootstrap, regional cell tables, summaries plots without rerunning fitting resampling. allocation article demonstrates supply scenario, export reload. Package help now explains compatibility public FCA older private allocation results. Older objects may require regeneration current prediction reporting; huff_decay results must relabeled corrected CLM outputs.
